verses.1: These are the names of the sons of Israel who, accompanied by their households, migrated with Jacob into Egypt:
verses.4: Dan and Naphtali; Gad and Asher.
verses.5: The total number of the direct descendants of Jacob was seventy. Joseph was already in Egypt.
verses.6: Now Joseph and all his brothers and that whole generation died.
verses.7: But the Israelites were fruitful and prolific. They became so numerous and strong that the land was filled with them.
verses.8: Then a new king, who knew nothing of Joseph, came to power in Egypt.
verses.9: He said to his subjects, "Look how numerous and powerful the Israelite people are growing, more so than we ourselves!
verses.10: Come, let us deal shrewdly with them to stop their increase; otherwise, in time of war they too may join our enemies to fight against us, and so leave our country."
verses.11: Accordingly, taskmasters were set over the Israelites to oppress them with forced labor. Thus they had to build for Pharaoh the supply cities of Pithom and Raamses.
verses.12: Yet the more they were oppressed, the more they multiplied and spread. The Egyptians, then, dreaded the Israelites
verses.13: and reduced them to cruel slavery,
verses.14: making life bitter for them with hard work in mortar and brick and all kinds of field work - the whole cruel fate of slaves.
verses.15: The king of Egypt told the Hebrew midwives, one of whom was called Shiphrah and the other Puah,
verses.16: When you act as midwives for the Hebrew women and see them giving birth, if it is a boy, kill him; but if it is a girl, she may live."
verses.17: The midwives, however, feared God; they did not do as the king of Egypt had ordered them, but let the boys live.
verses.18: So the king summoned the midwives and asked them, "Why have you acted thus, allowing the boys to live?"
verses.19: The midwives answered Pharaoh, "The Hebrew women are not like the Egyptian women. They are robust and give birth before the midwife arrives."
verses.20: Therefore God dealt well with the midwives. The people, too, increased and grew strong.
verses.21: And because the midwives feared God, he built up families for them.
verses.22: Pharaoh then commanded all his subjects, "Throw into the river every boy that is born to the Hebrews, but you may let all the girls live."

notes.text: Sons of Israel: here literally the first-generation sons of Jacob. Cf Genesis 1:5. However, beginning with Exodus 1:7 the same Hebrew phrase refers to the more remote descendants of Jacob; hence, from here on, it is ordinarily rendered "the Israelites." Households: the family in its fullest sense, including wives, children and servants.
The sons of Jacob are listed here according to the respective mothers. Cf Genesis 29:31; 30:20; 35:16-26
Direct descendants: literally, persons coming from the loins of Jacob; hence, wives and servants are here excluded. Cf Genesis 46:26
Who knew nothing of Joseph: this king ignored the services that Joseph had rendered to Egypt.
Pharaoh: not a personal name, but a title common to all the kings of Egypt.
Mortar: either the wet clay with which the bricks were made, as in Nahum 3:14, or the cement used between the bricks in building, as in Genesis 11:3
And see them giving birth: the Hebrew text is uncertain.
The river: the Nile, which was "the" river for the Egyptians.
